dedupe_keys.name: netbravo crowdsourced cellular wi fi and broadband measurements for europe jrc

description: netBravo was a crowdsourcing application of the European Commission's Joint Research Centre that measured mobile and Wi-Fi networks from volunteers' phones. The JRC publishes three open datasets from it, issued on 25 May 2016: European cellular signal strength coverage, European Wi-Fi hotspot signal strength coverage, and European broadband user experience (download and upload speed and ping over cellular and Wi-Fi). Each is aggregated on the ETRS89 statistical grid (GRID_ETRS89) at 100 m and 1 km resolution and delivered as a grid shapefile and CSV. Coverage: European countries where volunteers ran the app, mainly the mid-2010s. Format and access: ZIP files with shapefile and CSV from the JRC radio lab server, free of charge for commercial and non-commercial reuse under the Commission's reuse policy. Caveats: crowdsourced and uneven; biased to places and times where users measured; the Wi-Fi and cellular files were last modified in May 2026, but the broadband file answered 410 Gone and the netBravo site redirects. Simulation uses: observed signal strength to check modelled mobile coverage for hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related records: Ookla open tiles and OpenCelliD are larger crowdsourced sources; the Breitbandatlas and Arcep maps give official coverage.
